meta.description: Frontend-only map of the Overwatch match-tracker React app: every page and component down to individual UI elements (buttons, inputs, cards, charts, etc.), each carrying a copy-pasteable `grep` command that jumps straight to its exact source line. Intended both for Sean to click through in the browser and for Claude Code to read directly as a lookup table when asked to change a specific piece of UI.
meta.generated: frontend UI-element snapshot, extracted from live source (client/src) via parallel agent read + grep-verified anchors, at analysis time
meta.howToUse: Click a node to see its file and, for page/component nodes, a 'UI Elements' list. Each element's locate.grep is a ready-to-paste `grep -n -F -- "<anchor>" <file>` command — run it in the repo root (~/Code/overwatch) to land on the exact line. Uses plain grep (not ripgrep) deliberately: ripgrep isn't installed on this machine outside the Claude Code sandbox, so grep is what will actually work when pasted into a real terminal. locate.path is the file:line at extraction time as a secondary reference (may drift if the file is edited above that line; the grep command will not).
rules: An inspect id is unique across the whole app, not just within its own component or page. The overlay resolves the first element carrying an id and stops, so two elements sharing one id leaves the second unreachable. Worse, the inspector then reports an element the reader is not looking at, with a description that does not match what is on their screen. On 2026-09-20 in nfl-props the shortlist pill reused the card pill's id. A request to move one moved the other, and two rounds were spent describing different parts of the page to each other before the cause surfaced.

A function that emits an element and is called from more than one place must take its id as a parameter. Reusing markup is good; reusing the id that identifies it is not. This is the shape the 2026-09-20 duplicate took, and it is the one a uniqueness grep cannot catch, because the id appears exactly once in the source.
When one id is a prefix of others (prematch-rank-drum against prematch-rank-drum-up), anchor the grep on the full attribute so it cannot match a child.
Every entry here is added, renamed or removed in the same change as the element it describes. A map that lags the code is worse than no map: it answers confidently and wrongly.

uiElements.description: Step-1 card spanning two of the three page columns (2026-09-30 redesign; Today takes the third). Header: title, the offered-maps search (prematch-map-search-input, inline completion), "tap up to 3", and the picked map's type pill. Body is three columns: left = offered-map tiles + Clear, the vote advice (prematch-map-voting-card) spans the other two. The best/worst map tiles that held the third column were cut 2026-10-04 (split plan decision 5); the full map table is in the map drawer (mapDrawer-all-maps-table). uiElements.label: Vote advice (right two columns of the Map card)
uiElements.description: Right two thirds (col-span-2) of prematch-map-card since 2026-10-04; middle column from 2026-09-30 (was its own "Map Voting" card). Advice only: with maps offered, the first choice on top (map name large, role pill, hero - win% - games), then 2nd and 3rd stacked one line each (map name left, hero and win% right). With no maps offered it says "Enter the offered maps for a vote." (prematch-map-voting-empty). Ranking prefers the hero-informed testPick across offered maps x the testing hero pool, falling back to the map-only blended score; it ranks map x hero PAIRS, so one map can appear twice and another not at all (known, not fixed).

uiElements.label: Vote advice empty line

uiElements.label: Next test — mid-block lock line

Shown while nextTest.block is set, i.e. Sean has an open (unclosed, >0 minute) block on one hero — the card deliberately does NOT recompute the round-robin pick until the block closes. Unlike the old stint, an interruption (playing another hero and coming back) does not reset this — the block is derived from that hero's own whole credited history, not a run of consecutive matches.

Each column sorts like lib/nextTest.ts: cold (7+ days unplayed, COLD_DAYS) first, then least credited, then longest since last played. Rows are prematch-next-test-hero-row. Shown in every status branch, not just the recompute one.

, which never render together.

uiElements.description: Hero row progress: fills the bottom of the row as far as the open 60-minute block (or legacy games at this sens) has gone, with a straight vertical end (was a 20deg slant until 2026-09-30). Full strength on a tapped row, on hover otherwise.

uiElements.label: Hero picker stage/chunk watermark
uiElements.description: Oversized faded stage/chunk label (A1..B4) behind a hero row, centred (ink centre measured within 2px of the row centre; translate-x 0.15em corrects the italic lean). On a tapped row it is lit only as far as the progress fill reaches: the label spans the card width so --lit-x = fill x card width - 0.15em.

uiElements.label: Hero picker button
uiElements.description: One hero row in the Select Your Hero picker. Click toggles it into the match's pick order. Selected and hover states both use the ROLE's colour, not the brand accent — teal in the DPS column, pink in the Support column — via --sel set inline on every chip so hover and selection agree. Matches the order badge, which already coloured by role. The hero the Next test card points at (stint hero, else the top recommendation) gets .test-glow, a pulsing role-coloured halo. Styled like Log Match's mode tiles since 2026-09-27: selected = border-2 .is-selected.mode-fill with the name in .lit-text.lit-strong; resting = .hero-pane, the lobby slider's unlit rank-pane look in the role hue (1px border at 35%/15% light/dark + bottom tint), with 1px extra padding so selecting doesn't shift the row; --muted name (was --faint; games --faint, was --faint-2; brightened 2026-09-28) with NO hover brightening (removed 2026-09-27 as jarring). 4px corners both states. Name, win rate and games use the app's standard upright .hero-name face (Chakra Petch; italic dropped 2026-09-28). Win rate/games show this map's numbers once a map is picked and all maps' before that (GET /api/stats/prematch returns all-maps byHero when no map is sent); hidden only for a hero with 0 games. On a selected test card every letter (arrow, name, sens tag, win rate, games) glows only as far as the gauge reaches (.lit-fill); coloured numbers keep their own hue via .lit-hue.

uiElements.description: " @ <sens>" after a hero's name in Select Your Hero: the sens this hero's test is running at, or (emerald) the best sens its own testing settled on. Shown only when the hero has a sens test.

uiElements.label: Identity strip — account + role
uiElements.description: Page-level strip at the very top of Pre-Match holding both halves of 'who is playing right now': the four account pills (Pinx/Jinx/Winx/Linx) and the two role pills (DPS/Support), plus a right-aligned readout naming the active rank slot and its rank. Created 2026-09-19 by merging two controls that lived in different cards — account pills were in the Lobby Rank header, role pills in Map Voting's. Four things read the pair: the advisor request, the Hero Advisor card's role pill, Log Match's hero dropdown filter, and which of the eight rank slots the drum shows. It sits ABOVE the cards rather than inside one, and that is load-bearing: the Lobby Rank card is hidden entirely on Quickplay (queueMode === 'qp_role'), so folding role into it would have made the role pick vanish exactly when Quickplay needs it. Both pill groups render through one local identityPill() helper so the two choices cannot drift apart visually. Uses .card but overrides the VERTICAL half of its p-5 to zero — the pills span the bar edge to edge and define its height, with min-h-[34px] as the floor. Horizontal padding stays at the card's px-5 deliberately: the Sens Test card below shares that 20px inset, so 'Playing as' and that card's title start on the same vertical line. each group is a segmented control (identityGroup) with a single lit block that SLIDES between options rather than blinking off one and on to another. Three things make the step exact: auto-cols-fr equalises option widths within a group, and every button stacks all six labels (both groups) invisibly under its own so account and role pills share the width of the widest, 'Support'. So step N is always N x 100% of the indicator's width (no refs, nothing to re-measure on resize); there is NO gap between options, since a gap is not part of that 100% and the indicator would drift further out of register each step; and the indicator alone carries the border and .is-selected while the buttons carry only text, because two elements painting a border would double it mid-slide. Pills are full height with a 7px corner notch — half the .card's own 14px, the proportion used elsewhere on the page. The label and readout use self-center so they do not stretch with the pills. Its 'Playing as' label uses .card-title, the same class as every card heading, so the strip reads as a section of the page rather than stray text. The two pill groups are centred in the strip, done by giving the 'Playing as' label and the rank readout `flex-1 basis-0` rather than by margins — equal basis makes both side items claim equal width whatever they contain, so the centre does not drift when the readout's rank text changes length. Layout since 2026-10-01: a 10-column grid on a 4-2-4 split (Sean's spec). Left 4: 'Playing as', the account pills, and the rank-slot readout. Middle 2: the role pick, whose column keeps its space even in Open Queue where the pick is hidden. Right 4: the role timer. The rank-slot readout was removed the same day (Sean). All text in the strip shares the pills' baseline: labels are wrapped in onLine(), a 12px line-height-1 box centred like the pill text, and the timer bar is an inline-block sitting on that baseline.

uiElements.label: Role timer (Playing As slip, right column)
uiElements.description: Role timer, the right column (4 of 10) of the Playing As slip. A faint 'Role time' label, then a role-coloured progress bar that stretches across the column, then the readout (e.g. 'DPS 3h 36m / 4h'). At 240 min (ROLE_THRESHOLD_MIN in server/src/lib/roleTimer.ts) the readout reads '4h — switch to Support'. Hover title carries the fine print (comp only, match count, since date). Shown in every queue mode. Reads GET /api/role-timer; refetches on matchLoggedSignal and revalidateAll. Quick Play ignored. Since 2026-10-02 the clock follows a detour/real-switch rule (see header of roleTimer.ts): a lone other-role match between two same-role runs is dropped; a run of 2+ resets the old role; a lone newest new-role match is 'pending' and the readout appends '<role> held at Xh Ym, one more <new role> resets it' from the response's `held` field. Recommendation only. Added 2026-10-01.

uiElements.label: Role timer progress bar
uiElements.description: Track of the progress bar, total minutes over the 240-minute threshold.

uiElements.label: Role timer progress fill
uiElements.description: Filled part of the bar, coloured with the current role's ROLE_SEL_RGB hue, capped at 100%.

uiElements.label: Role timer readout
uiElements.description: 'DPS 3h 36m / 4h', plus '(+Nm est.)' only when estimated minutes exist (comp matches without Aim Stats minutes, counted at the average). At or over threshold: '4h — switch to Support'. Sits after the bar.

uiElements.label: Identity strip — Account label
uiElements.description: Small faint uppercase label just left of the account picker. Added 2026-09-24, same style as the Today label on the Hero Advisor dots.

uiElements.label: Identity strip — Role label
uiElements.description: Small faint uppercase label just left of the DPS/Support picker, in the strip's middle column. Added 2026-09-24, same style as the Account label.

uiElements.label: Identity strip — account picker
uiElements.description: Row of four pills in the page-level identity strip (moved there from the Lobby Rank header on 2026-09-19), one per Overwatch account: Pinx, Jinx, Winx, Linx (renamed from SOJ/SKI/26R/26J the same day). Added 2026-09-19. Styled from Map Voting's role pills — same clipped corner and the shared .is-selected bottom-lit state — because it is the same kind of control. The selected pill takes the hue of that account's current rank tier via --sel, so the pill row and the rank badge below agree. Switching accounts swaps the whole rank context: player_rank and the lobby range are stored per account AND per role — EIGHT slots — under 'ow-player-rank:<ACCT>:<Role>' and 'ow-lobby-range:<ACCT>:<Role>', read (not cleared) on switch, so every slot keeps where it was left. The role half comes from Role Pick on the Map Voting card; prematch-lobby-rank-slot-label names the active pairing. Both swaps happen inside the setters, not in an effect — an effect runs after the lobby-persist effect and would copy the outgoing slot's range onto the incoming slot's key. Pre-split values migrate once to Linx/Support (Sean's statement 2026-09-19 that the stored rank was Linx's support rank), guarded by 'ow-rank-migrated-to-role-slots' so a legitimate clear is not undone. NOTE: the account name IS the storage key suffix, so a future rename strands that account's stored rank and range — only the default is covered by the legacy adoption. NOTE: the account is NOT written to the matches table — no schema change was made; a logged match still records only player_rank. Rendered by identityGroup as a sliding segmented control; the lit block's hue transitions with the slide, so moving from a Gold account to a Platinum one changes colour as it travels.

uiElements.label: Account — Pinx
uiElements.description: Selects the Pinx account. Loads that account's stored rank into the drum and its stored lobby range into the track; nothing is cleared, so switching back restores what was there.

uiElements.label: Account — Jinx
uiElements.description: Selects the Jinx account. Loads that account's stored rank into the drum and its stored lobby range into the track; nothing is cleared, so switching back restores what was there.

uiElements.label: Account — Winx
uiElements.description: Selects the Winx account. Loads that account's stored rank into the drum and its stored lobby range into the track; nothing is cleared, so switching back restores what was there.

uiElements.label: Account — Linx
uiElements.description: Selects the Linx account. Loads that account's stored rank into the drum and its stored lobby range into the track; nothing is cleared, so switching back restores what was there.

uiElements.label: Lobby range slider
uiElements.description: The lobby's rank spread, as a band on a track. The track is one cell per division, reaching 10 divisions either side of Sean's rank. The band's left edge is the lobby floor, its right edge the ceiling. Nothing is drawn until Sean presses the track — a band that appeared on its own would be a guess dressed as an observation. The bar persists across matches as of 2026-09-19 — it is no longer wiped on submit, Reset or Match Cancelled, because consecutive matches are nearly always the same lobby. It clears only via this component's own 'clear' button, or when the rank drum moves.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — floor handle
uiElements.description: Left end of the bar: a triangle pointing outward, so the shape says which way to pull. Drag it to move only the lobby floor. Drawn with clip-path and lit with drop-shadow, which follows the clipped silhouette — box-shadow would draw a rectangle around a triangle. Its grab area is 24px, larger than the 10px arrowhead, so it can be hit on a trackpad. The lane owns the gesture; this element only declares its role.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — ceiling handle
uiElements.description: Right end of the bar: a triangle pointing outward. Drag it to move only the lobby ceiling. Same clip-path drawing, oversized grab area and role-only arrangement as the floor handle.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — width readout
uiElements.description: Band width in divisions. Persisted to localStorage 'ow-lobby-tray-width' and reused next match; the band's POSITION is never remembered.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — narrow by one
uiElements.description: Shrinks the band one division, keeping it centred where it already sits.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — widen by one
uiElements.description: Grows the band one division, keeping it centred where it already sits.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — clear
uiElements.description: Removes the band, returning the range to unrecorded. Only shown once a band exists.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — tier label row
uiElements.description: Tier names above the boxes, each spanning its own run. Short runs near the ends of the row fall back to the tier's initial.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — box row
uiElements.description: One box per division, tinted by tier, printed with the division number. The boxes are panes of tinted glass and the bar below is a near-UV lamp: a pane the bar sits under FLUORESCES — a sliver of raw violet at the contact edge, then its own tier colour taking over and carrying all the way to the top edge rather than dying halfway. Unlit panes drop to near-transparent, which is what makes the lit ones read as lit. Sean's own rank carries an inset ring. Clicking a box drops the bar centred on it.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — single rank box
uiElements.description: One division. Click places the bar centred here at the remembered width. A lit pane gathers light at its left and right edges and bleeds it sideways into the gaps; the two panes at the ends of the lit run bleed twice as far, since they are the only ones with darkness beside them to bleed into.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — bar lane
uiElements.description: The strip beneath the boxes that holds the bar, and the sole owner of the drag gesture — it captures the pointer and reads what was grabbed off the target's data-drag-role. Pressing bare lane moves the bar there, centred. Shares the boxes' CSS grid so the bar's ends land on box edges exactly.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — sliding bar
uiElements.description: The light bar: the reading itself, sitting under the boxes the lobby spanned. A cold lamp — near-white core bleeding into the theme's secondary accent, ow.blue #29D3F2 — with three stacked blooms. Colours come from LAMP_GLOW/LAMP_CONTACT at the top of the file, so the lamp is one edit, not a dozen. The core stays near-white on purpose: a lamp saturated all the way through tints every pane its own hue and undoes what the tiers are for. Drag it to move; arrow keys move it one division, shift+arrow stretches its right end.

uiElements.label: Lobby range — halo above the lit boxes
uiElements.description: Decorative. The light that made it through the glass and kept going, drawn one blurred segment PER LIT COLUMN and tinted by that column's tier — the colour is created by the pane, not by the lamp. Sits above the box row, fading upward. Pointer-events-none and aria-hidden.

uiElements.label: Today's results line
uiElements.description: One continuous 4px line flush on the Today stats box's bottom border, the box's full inner width, split into equal segments, one per game today, most recent left, flat emerald/red. Empty grey track when no games. Clipped to the box's rounded corners.

uiElements.label: Today results segment
uiElements.description: One game's segment of the Today results line; hover shows result, hero and map.

nodes.label: LogMatch.tsx
nodes.description: Match logging form: Deaths card (buffered per-death killer/role/ult facts), Match Details card (date/time/hero/map/mode/result/sens/feel-slider/team-rating/match-quality/result-driver/notes, Log Match button), and a Recently Logged card listing today's entries. uiElements.label: Deaths card
uiElements.description: Card that owns the whole in-match death flow: two columns from lg up — the list of deaths buffered so far on the left, the inline DeathLogger capture control on the right (a 'Log a death' button that expands a compact MRU/role-tab/hero-grid picker in place; it was a fixed bottom-right skull FAB until 2026-09-10), stacked history-then-picker below lg, so a growing list never pushes the capture control down the screen — killer hero, killer role, and an inline ⚡ ult toggle per row — with a Clear all action and per-death remove. The buffer flushes to match_deaths on submit.

uiElements.label: Clear all (deaths) button
uiElements.description: Button shown only when deaths are buffered; clears the entire in-progress death buffer for the current match.

uiElements.label: Deaths card — history column
uiElements.description: Left column of the Deaths card (full width when stacked below lg): holds the buffered death list, or the 'log each death as it happens' empty state.

uiElements.label: Deaths card — capture column
uiElements.description: Right column of the Deaths card (stacks below the history column under lg): holds the DeathLogger picker, sticky from lg up so it stays in view as the death list grows.

uiElements.label: Death buffer list
uiElements.description: List of deaths logged so far this match (fact-only capture, 2026-09-09 on) — each row shows the killer hero and role, an inline ⚡ toggle to mark/unmark the death as an ult kill, and an x button to remove that entry from the buffer.

uiElements.label: Death row ult toggle (⚡)
uiElements.description: Per-row toggle in the Deaths card buffer list that flips a buffered death's ult flag after the fact — never part of the tap-to-log path itself, since the ~10s respawn window only allows one tap for who killed you.

uiElements.label: Match Details card
uiElements.description: Card containing the match-logging form; its header includes the Reset button that clears hero, notes, map, and feel.

uiElements.label: Match Cancelled button
uiElements.description: Cancels the match currently being built: clears hero, notes, map, feel, team rating, and the death buffer (with a confirm prompt if any deaths were already tracked), and calls notifyMatchLogged() with no args so Prematch's Map Voting picks reset too (bumps matchLoggedSignal without setting lastLog, so it doesn't also trigger the win/loss flash overlay). Sits top-right in the Match Details card header, paired with the Game crashed toggle (same pill size and style); it also clears the win/loss result and the death buffer. Then smooth-scrolls the window to the very top of the page and focuses the map search input with preventScroll, so focus doesn't pull the page back down.

uiElements.label: Match Details form
uiElements.description: The full match-logging form (date, time, sensitivity display, hero, map, mode, result, notes, feel) that POSTs a new match to /api/matches on submit.

uiElements.label: Date input
uiElements.description: Date picker for the match being logged; defaults to today and auto-advances with the clock until the user hand-edits it (backfill).

uiElements.label: Time input
uiElements.description: Time picker for the match being logged; defaults to the current clock time and stops auto-following once hand-edited (backfill).

uiElements.label: Sensitivity display
uiElements.description: Read-only display of the in-game sensitivity this match will actually be logged at: the picked hero's active DPI test stage value if one's running (Competitive, or Quickplay-as-Support), otherwise the frozen fallback sens. Not editable from this form.

uiElements.label: 1st hero select
uiElements.description: Dropdown grouped by role (DPS/Tank/Support) for choosing the match's starting hero (pre-filled from the Pre-Match picker); each option shows today's play count for that hero. First of three hero slots — see logmatch-hero-switch-select-2/3 for the optional mid-match switches, all of which share the match's result on submit.

uiElements.label: 2nd hero select (mid-match switch)
uiElements.description: Optional second hero slot for a mid-match hero switch; grouped by role like the 1st hero select. The logged result and death buffer apply to every filled hero slot, not just the first.

uiElements.label: 3rd hero select (mid-match switch)
uiElements.description: Optional third hero slot for a second mid-match hero switch; grouped by role like the 1st hero select. uiElements.label: Hero role badge
uiElements.description: Colored pill (DPS/Tank/Support) that appears under the Hero select once a hero has been chosen, reflecting that hero's role.

uiElements.label: Map type badge
uiElements.description: Pill showing the selected map's type (e.g. Control, Escort, Hybrid, Push) next to the map name.

uiElements.description: Read-only "Recording as {queue}" line at the top of the Match Details form (2026-09-29): the queue is chosen once on the mode tiles and the log form no longer re-asks it (design-language section 7). uiElements.label: Change queue link
uiElements.description: The "change" link next to the Recording as chip. Scrolls back to the mode tiles (#sec-mode) where the queue is chosen.

uiElements.label: Game crashed toggle
uiElements.description: Pill on the right of the Recording as line (2026-10-02). On = the match is logged result-only: hero, sens, feel, team, match quality, result driver, aim-stats fold-out and the Deaths card are hidden and not sent; role comes from Playing As. uiElements.label: Crashed match role line
uiElements.description: Replaces the Hero row while Game crashed is on: shows the role the match is recorded under (taken from Playing As).

uiElements.label: Result toggle (Win/Loss)
uiElements.description: Win/Loss toggle with an animated sliding fill and chevron rank-insignia buttons; selecting Win or Loss sets the outcome to be logged for this match.

uiElements.label: Main Perceived Factors textarea
uiElements.description: Free-text field for notes on perceived factors affecting the match (e.g. fatigue, warmup, stage change), saved with the logged match. Rendered via the generic RegistryField component (client/src/components/RegistryField.tsx) as of 2026-09-23's field-registry contract freeze — re-anchored on the field-id call site since the actual <textarea> and its data-inspect-id now live in RegistryField.tsx, not here.

uiElements.label: Feel slider(s)
uiElements.description: One range slider (0-100) per filled hero slot, capturing whether the sensitivity felt floaty (slow) or jittery (fast), snappy in the middle, on that hero during this specific match — captured live since the sensation fades before the next match. Container is logmatch-feel-sliders; each individual input shares this same data-inspect-id.

uiElements.label: Rank outcome row (required)
uiElements.description: Sits directly above the Log Match button and is REQUIRED on a ranked match that has a rank set — the submit button stays disabled until one of the two options is chosen. A match that moved the ladder and one that did not are different facts, and leaving it unanswered used to record 'no change' silently, which is how a derank goes missing. Border turns accent while unanswered and a 'required' tag shows. With no rank set it does not gate: there is nothing to choose between, so it tells Sean to go set one instead of trapping the form. Hidden on quickplay.

uiElements.label: Current rank badge (log page)
uiElements.description: The shared RankBadge at small size, reading the live server rank from player_ranks. Same component as prematch-rank-drum-badge, so pressing a button in this row moves the Pre-Match badge too.

uiElements.label: Promoted/Demoted + No change
uiElements.description: Two options, never three: only a loss can demote and only a win can promote, so the first button reads 'Promoted' on a win and 'Demoted' on a loss. Selected state uses the same is-selected treatment as the Match quality and Result driver toggles.

uiElements.label: Promoted / Demoted
uiElements.description: Writes the new rank as start rank plus or minus one division, through PUT /api/ranks, so every surface sees it. Label follows the match result. Changing the result afterwards clears the answer and puts the rank back, so a promotion cannot be left standing on a loss.

uiElements.label: No change
uiElements.description: Answers the required question without moving the ladder, and restores the rank if a direction was picked first. player_rank_start and player_rank then match on the saved row, which is what stops a mark being drawn.

uiElements.label: Log Match button
uiElements.description: Primary submit button that saves the match to the database (POST /api/matches); shows Saving…/✓ Saved states and is disabled until hero, map, result, date, and sens are all valid.

uiElements.label: Add aim stats now fold-out

Appears only for a match that would land in the Awaiting Stats backlog (Competitive, hero not a Designated Fallback, an active test set covering the hero). Open and filled: POST /api/matches carries an aim_stats block and the server saves match + stats in one transaction, so the match never enters the backlog. Closed or blank: unchanged, the match waits in the backlog.

uiElements.label: Aim stats fold-out toggle
uiElements.description: Header row of the fold-out; click to open/close. The closed label hints that skipping sends the match to Awaiting Stats.

uiElements.label: Aim stats fold-out body
uiElements.description: Expanded body: the shared per-hero stat fields plus the combat scoreboard. One stat row per hero played (rebuilt when the switch heroes change, keeping typed values).

uiElements.label: Aim stats incomplete hint
uiElements.description: Shown only when stats are partly filled but invalid (needs a duration for every hero and the first hero's overall accuracy); the Log Match button stays disabled until fixed or cleared.

uiElements.label: Fold-out hero accuracy + duration rows
uiElements.description: One row per hero played with duration, accuracy, crit and extra-accuracy fields. Same StatFields component (components/AimStatsFields.tsx) as the Sens page's Record combat details form, with its ids prefixed `logmatch-aim`.

uiElements.label: Fold-out per-hero duration input
uiElements.description: Required m:ss duration for a played hero. Same StatFields component (components/AimStatsFields.tsx) as the Sens page's Record combat details form, with its ids prefixed `logmatch-aim`.

uiElements.label: Fold-out overall accuracy input
uiElements.description: Overall accuracy % (label varies per hero). Same StatFields component (components/AimStatsFields.tsx) as the Sens page's Record combat details form, with its ids prefixed `logmatch-aim`.

uiElements.label: Fold-out crit accuracy input
uiElements.description: Crit accuracy % for heroes that have a crit slot. Same StatFields component (components/AimStatsFields.tsx) as the Sens page's Record combat details form, with its ids prefixed `logmatch-aim`.

uiElements.label: Fold-out extra accuracy input
uiElements.description: Hero-specific extra accuracy slot. Same StatFields component (components/AimStatsFields.tsx) as the Sens page's Record combat details form, with its ids prefixed `logmatch-aim`.

uiElements.description: Added 2026-09-24. One editable number input per switch-hero slot (2nd/3rd), prefilled from match_heroes.sens via GET /api/matches/:id/heroes. Disabled when its hero slot is empty. A blank field means 'don't touch this hero's sens' — on Save it's omitted rather than written as null. Save logic (client/src/lib/matchEditRoster.ts, buildRosterEditPayload): if the slot-2/3 roster is unchanged this session, the value goes through `heroSens` (hero-keyed, same field SensLog.tsx's backfill form uses), which never re-runs the server's stage-credit recompute; if the roster DID change (a hero added/removed/swapped), it rides along on the full `heroes` replace instead, where a hero under an active stage test can still have its sens recomputed — existing behavior, unchanged.

uiElements.label: 2nd/3rd hero sens — credited test game warning (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Added 2026-09-24. Same notice as logmatch-inline-edit-slot1-sens-credit-warning, per switch-hero slot. In practice should never render — only the starting hero (slot 1) can ever earn a blind_credits row (2026-09-24 rule in matches.ts) — but reads the server's actual `credited` join rather than assuming, so it stays correct if that rule ever changes.

uiElements.label: Map select (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Map select inside a Today's Matches row's inline edit form, with a map-type pill shown once a map is picked.

uiElements.label: Result: Win (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Win/Loss result buttons inside a Today's Matches row's inline edit form. (Locate command matches both Win and Loss buttons.)

uiElements.label: Result: Loss (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Win/Loss result buttons inside a Today's Matches row's inline edit form. (Rendered by the same map as logmatch-inline-edit-result-win — locate command matches both.)

uiElements.label: Rank outcome (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Demoted / No change / Promoted fix for a Today's Matches row, with the start → end rank it produces. Saves through PUT /api/matches/:id/rank-outcome, which also shifts every later game on that account+role and the live rank (stops at a game already hand-fixed). Hidden on quickplay and Tank.

uiElements.label: Rank outcome: Demoted (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: One of the three rank-outcome buttons in a Today's Matches row's inline edit form. (Locate command matches all three.)

uiElements.label: Rank outcome: No change (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: One of the three rank-outcome buttons in a Today's Matches row's inline edit form. (Locate command matches all three.)

uiElements.label: Rank outcome: Promoted (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: One of the three rank-outcome buttons in a Today's Matches row's inline edit form. (Locate command matches all three.)

uiElements.label: Leaver side toggle (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Added 2026-09-24 (ported from MatchEditDrawer.tsx, same day the coordinator confirmed this inline form is the live edit surface). Same sliver control as the main Log Match form's logmatch-leaver-side-toggle, rendered here by the shared LeaverSliver.tsx component with dataInspectPrefix="logmatch-inline-edit-leaver-side". Prefilled from this row's leaver/leaver_side (already present on the Today's Matches list row via GET /api/matches' SELECT *). Handles a historical row logged before leaver_side existed (leaver=1, side never recorded): neither sliver lights up and the label reads 'Leaver — side not recorded' instead of implying no leaver; only an actual tap resolves it (`leaverUnknown` state), so an untouched Save preserves the original row.

uiElements.label: Leaver side option (mine/theirs, inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Added 2026-09-24. One of the two sliver buttons inside logmatch-inline-edit-leaver-side-toggle. Rendered by LeaverSliver.tsx — anchor points at the same LogMatch.tsx call site.

uiElements.label: Leaver side small-print label (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Added 2026-09-24. One caption under each bar: 'Enemy Leaver - Free win?' (left) and 'Friendly Leaver - GG go next' (right); the picked side's caption is .lit-text, lit from above (brightest at the top, next to its bar). An untouched historical unknown-side row shows a single centred 'Leaver — side not recorded' instead. Rendered by LeaverSliver.tsx — anchor points at the same LogMatch.tsx call site.

uiElements.label: Save Changes button (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Saves hero/map/result/mid-match-switch-hero edits for this match via PUT /api/matches/:id, then calls revalidateAll and collapses the row. Disabled while saving or if hero/map is unset.

uiElements.label: Delete this match button (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Starts the delete flow for this match; requires a second tap on logmatch-inline-edit-confirm-delete-button to actually DELETE /api/matches/:id.

uiElements.label: Confirm delete button (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: Shown after tapping Delete this match; confirms the DELETE /api/matches/:id call.

uiElements.label: Queue mode toggle (inline edit form)
uiElements.description: iOS-style switch (blue "Q"/red "C" flanking labels) inside a Today's Matches row's inline edit form. Clicking it PUTs a queue_mode flip (qp_role ↔ comp_role) to /api/matches/:id and calls revalidateAll. Disabled for Competitive Open matches (switch only knows QP and Comp Role; change Open from the full edit drawer). Comp -> QP prompts a window.confirm first — that direction rolls back the match's DPI-test stage credit (drops its blind_credits row server-side) and removes it from the Sens page's Awaiting Stats list. Moved here from an overlay on the collapsed row's watermark, now that the row expands into a full edit form instead.

uiElements.label: Nothing logged today empty state
uiElements.description: Empty-state message shown in the Today's Matches card when no matches have been logged yet for the current day.

uiElements.label: Team rating stars
uiElements.description: Perceived teammate-quality rating, 0-5 stars in half-star steps, captured live at log time. Rendered via the generic RegistryField component (client/src/components/RegistryField.tsx) as of 2026-09-23's field-registry contract freeze — re-anchored on the field-id call site since the actual <StarRating> and its data-inspect-id now live in RegistryField.tsx, not here.

uiElements.label: Match quality segmented control
uiElements.description: Stomp/Close two-option toggle — a fact about how decisive the score was, not a judgment. Starts unselected and stays null if untouched; clicking the selected option again deselects it.

uiElements.label: Match quality option button
uiElements.description: One of the two Stomp/Close buttons inside the match-quality toggle.

uiElements.label: Result driver segmented control
uiElements.description: Me/Team two-option toggle — collective-effort vs. individually-decided, NOT a rating of teammates ('Team' includes Sean himself). Starts unselected and stays null if untouched; clicking the selected option again deselects it.

uiElements.label: Result driver option button
uiElements.description: One of the two Me/Team buttons inside the result-driver toggle.

uiElements.label: Result Win/Loss buttons
uiElements.description: Two buttons in the app's shared selected style. Win carries teal, Loss pink, via --sel; .is-selected draws the bottom-lit treatment. Replaced a sliding fill and an animated chevron insignia, whose 'is-selected' class name collided with the new shared one.

uiElements.label: Result — one option (Win or Loss)
uiElements.description: Sets the match result. Selected shows the bottom-lit state in its own hue; unselected previews that hue on hover via .hover-sel.

uiElements.label: Leaver side toggle
uiElements.description: Two thin sliver buttons directly below the Win/Loss row, each spanning one result button: enemy leaver (left, under Win, muted teal) and friendly leaver (right, under Loss, muted pink). A lit bar gets .leaver-lamp: tinted fill with an inner glow rising from the bottom edge, no outer glow. Replaced the old square Leaver checkbox 2026-09-24 — which team the leaver was on matters more than a bare yes/no. Tap the selected side again to clear back to 'no leaver'. Extracted into the shared LeaverSliver.tsx component 2026-09-24 (same day MatchEditDrawer needed an identical control) — the id itself is built there from a `dataInspectPrefix` prop, so the anchor below points at LogMatch's call site, which passes dataInspectPrefix="logmatch-leaver-side".

uiElements.label: Score (us - them)
uiElements.description: Added 2026-10-04. Two small number inputs for the final round score, shared ScoreInputs.tsx. Blank saves NULL; whole numbers 0-10 (server 400s otherwise). Writes matches.score_us / score_them via POST /api/matches (Log Match) or PUT /api/matches/:id (drawer, prefilled from GET /api/matches/:id). Hidden for a crashed game.

uiElements.label: Leaver side option (mine/theirs)
uiElements.description: One of the two sliver buttons inside logmatch-leaver-side-toggle. Shared id across both (mine/theirs) — same convention as the identity-group toggles elsewhere on this app. Selected state lights with .leaver-lamp in its side's muted Win/Loss hue (SIDE_HUES in LeaverSliver.tsx); tapping the already-selected one clears leaverSide back to null. Rendered by LeaverSliver.tsx (see logmatch-leaver-side-toggle) — anchor points at the same LogMatch.tsx call site.

uiElements.label: Leaver side small-print label
uiElements.description: Tiny captions, one under each leaver-side sliver: 'Enemy Leaver - Free win?' (left, under Win) and 'Friendly Leaver - GG go next' (right, under Loss). The picked side's caption is .lit-text, lit from above (brightest at the top, next to its bar). Rendered by LeaverSliver.tsx (see logmatch-leaver-side-toggle) — anchor points at the same LogMatch.tsx call site.

nodes.label: SensLog.tsx
nodes.description: Sensitivity-study control page: per-hero DPI stage-trial plan grid with Create/Cancel test buttons and phase tabs, the active DPI stage card with a 'Get next stage' advance control, an ad-hoc test-set creation card, a DPI stage results table, and the post-match combat-stats backfill area — an Awaiting Stats column (matches still missing combat details, expand-in-place to enter them) beside a Logged Today column (today's already-saved matches, expand-in-place to review/correct them).

uiElements.label: Overall accuracy % input
uiElements.description: Required percent input for a played hero's overall accuracy stat — one row per hero played (a mid-match switch gets one row per hero, since time-on-hero varies).

uiElements.label: Crit accuracy % input
uiElements.description: Optional percent input for a played hero's crit accuracy — one row per hero played, same multi-hero layout as sl-overall-acc-input. Hidden entirely for heroes in NO_CRIT_HEROES (Juno), whose kit has no crit reading.

uiElements.label: Juno torpedo damage/healing inputs
uiElements.description: Per-hero raw scoreboard counts (whole numbers, not percentages) rendered from RAW_STAT_FIELDS — currently Juno only: Torpedo Damage and Torpedo Healing. Saved to aim_stats_heroes.torpedo_damage/torpedo_healing rather than the accuracy slots, which are averaged across heroes. data-inspect-ids are generated per field (sl-torpedo-damage-input, sl-torpedo-healing-input).

uiElements.label: Combat stats inputs (Elims/Deaths/Damage[/Healing])
uiElements.description: Endgame-scoreboard number inputs — Eliminations, Deaths, Damage, plus Healing when any played hero is a Support — for the match being recorded. Final blows was dropped from this set.

uiElements.label: SensNav sub-navigation
uiElements.description: Renders the shared Sensitivity-section sub-navigation bar (defined in components/SensNav) at the top of the page.

uiElements.label: "Sensitivity Study" page header
uiElements.description: Top-of-page h1 title and intro paragraph describing the sensitivity-study workflow.

uiElements.label: Phase overview card
uiElements.description: Compact status view of the current sens-study phase, reading the same GET /api/blind/next as Prematch's Next test card (server/src/lib/nextTest.ts) but showing every hero, not just the recommended role. Fixed at queue_mode=comp_role since this page is a status overview, not tied to what Sean is about to queue. Gated on the sens-study field-registry category. Shown only while at least one hero is pending (allFinished false and heroes non-empty) — sl-phase-overview-finished covers the other case.

uiElements.label: Phase overview — per-hero grid
uiElements.description: Two-column grid, one row per hero in the current phase (sl-phase-overview-hero-row), each showing days since last played, a cold badge (7+ days, mirrors lib/nextTest.ts's COLD_DAYS as a display-only threshold), and credited/target or a Done badge.

uiElements.label: Phase overview — per-hero row
uiElements.description: One row per hero in nextTest.heroes. Shared id across rows (each row's content, not a unique DOM id, is what distinguishes it) — see the map's own duplicate-id rule.

uiElements.label: Phase overview — all-finished notice
uiElements.description: Shown when nextTest.allFinished — every hero in the phase has completed its set. Nudges toward creating the next phase below (PlanCard's + Add new phase) without auto-creating one or choosing sens values.

uiElements.label: Mouse acceleration curve card
uiElements.description: The Rawaccel lookup table card (GET/PUT /api/aim/curve). Primary control is sl-lut-editor: Sean pastes the table straight out of Rawaccel and it is stamped on every match he logs afterwards (matches.curve_lut), so a retune becomes its own curve variant on the analysis page instead of blending into the old one. The smooth/input/output grid below it is the legacy Jump shape, demoted 2026-09-20 and no longer stamped on anything. The stage-test lock and its badge were removed the same day — editing the Jump fields can no longer change what any match ran under. Rendered above the Backfill panel.

uiElements.label: LUT point rows
uiElements.description: The table's points, as chips that wrap across the card. Each chip is one point: a speed in counts/ms and the multiplier applied once that speed is reached. Laid out inline rather than as full-width rows because no value here exceeds four digits — a 1fr column would be almost entirely empty space. These are the live editable fields; the Jump smooth/input/output grid that used to sit below was removed 2026-09-20 as useless.

uiElements.label: LUT point chip
uiElements.description: One point of the table: the speed box, a comma, the multiplier box, and a remove ×. The × is held at opacity 0 rather than hidden when only two points remain, so chip widths do not jump as points are added and removed.

uiElements.label: Point speed input
uiElements.description: Mouse speed in counts per millisecond. Must increase down the table; parseLutString rejects an out-of-order or repeated speed rather than guessing the intent.

uiElements.label: Point multiplier input
uiElements.description: What sensitivity is multiplied by once that speed is reached.

uiElements.label: Remove point
uiElements.description: Deletes that row. Disabled at 2 rows — a one-point table is not a curve.

uiElements.label: Add point
uiElements.description: Appends a row seeded 10 counts/ms past the last one, at the same multiplier. Capped at 32, matching the server bound.

uiElements.label: Paste from Rawaccel toggle
uiElements.description: Opens the bulk-entry box for filling every row at once from Rawaccel's own text.

uiElements.label: Copy table button
uiElements.description: Copies the table on screen — not the saved one — to the clipboard in Rawaccel's tight 'x,y;x,y' form, ready to paste into its LUT field. Copying the on-screen rows is the point: after tuning a value the reason to copy is to carry the NEW table across. Disabled while the rows do not parse.

uiElements.label: LUT bulk paste panel
uiElements.description: Collapsible bulk-entry panel. Fills the rows above; it does not save on its own.

uiElements.label: LUT paste box
uiElements.description: Takes Rawaccel's 'x,y;x,y' text. Parsed by parseLutString in client/src/lib/lut.ts, the same validator the rows use.

uiElements.label: Fill the rows button
uiElements.description: Parses the pasted text into the row fields. Leaves the result unsaved so it can be checked first.

uiElements.label: Revert LUT edits
uiElements.description: Restores the rows to the saved table. Only shown while there are unsaved changes and a table exists to revert to.

uiElements.label: LUT summary line
uiElements.description: Point count and top speed, plus an amber 'unsaved' marker while the rows differ from what is stored.

uiElements.label: LUT editor
uiElements.description: Wraps the whole lookup-table control: the stored table, the paste/edit box, and the save/clear actions. Writes curve_params.lut_points via PUT /api/aim/curve; lut_steps and lut_max_speed are derived from the pasted points, never typed.

uiElements.label: 'N points on file' badge
uiElements.description: Shown in the card header when a table is stored. Its absence is meaningful — see sl-lut-missing-badge.

uiElements.label: 'no table on file' badge
uiElements.description: Amber header badge shown when curve_params.lut_points is null. Matches logged in this state record only that acceleration was on, not what it was set to, so this is a real data gap rather than a cosmetic empty state.

uiElements.label: LUT parse error
uiElements.description: Names why a pasted table was rejected (too few points, non-numeric value, speeds not increasing). Save stays disabled while it shows.

uiElements.label: Save table button
uiElements.description: Writes the parsed points, with lutSteps = point count and lutMaxSpeed = largest x. Disabled until the box parses.

uiElements.label: Clear table button
uiElements.description: Sets lut_points back to null. Only shown when a table is stored. Matches logged afterwards go back to recording nothing about the curve shape.

uiElements.label: LUT save error
uiElements.description: Server-side rejection from PUT /api/aim/curve (bounds on steps or max speed), as opposed to the client-side parse failure above.

uiElements.label: "Sens stage trials" section header
uiElements.description: Section header introducing the stage-trial plan and testing area below the backfill panel. Renamed from "DPI stage trials" — mouse DPI is now locked at 1600 permanently and stages vary in-game sens instead.

uiElements.label: Phase plan card (Phase 2+ reference)
uiElements.description: Card showing the selected phase's per-hero DPI/sens test plan, with phase tabs (including a trailing "+ Add new phase" tab), a description line, and one status tile per hero.

uiElements.label: Mouse Accel ON badge
uiElements.description: Shown next to the phase description whenever the selected phase tab has curveEnabled set — flags that every hero test set in this phase was (or should be) played with Rawaccel acceleration on. Phase 7 is retroactively marked this way.

uiElements.label: Phase tabs (Phase 2, 3, 4, ... + Add new phase)
uiElements.description: Tab row switching which phase's per-hero test plan is displayed in the plan card. Hardcoded phases (Phase 2-5) come from PLAN_TABS in source; phases created via the "+ Add new phase" form are appended after them and persisted to localStorage. The trailing "+ Add new phase" button opens sl-add-phase-modal instead of switching tabs.

uiElements.label: Fallback order strip (banned/taken → who instead)
uiElements.description: Sits under the phase description, above the hero grid. Lists the phase's heroes split by role, in plan order — which IS rank order, most- to least-informative — so when a hero is banned or picked first, the next name down in the same role is the answer. Finished blocks are struck through; the first unfinished hero per role is bolded as next up. Derived from the plan plus statusForHero, not a separate hardcoded list. Sens proximity is deliberately not the ordering: each hero's bracket is its own, and changing sens between matches has no measurable cost (accuracy p=0.89). On custom phases only (key starts with custom-), a "+ Add hero" control at the bottom opens an inline form to append a hero to the end of the phase plan.

uiElements.label: Add-hero form (fallback strip)
uiElements.description: Right column of the fallback strip, beside the role lists. Hero picker (excludes heroes in the plan and retired ones), archetype dropdown (Hitscan / Projectile / Hybrid), range source (Default = the archetype's Phase 4 best-guess bracket from ARCHETYPE_DEFAULT_RANGE, read-only; Manual = type low/high), note. No block-length field: the server gives the new hero the same block length as the phase's first hero (minutes model). Sens is spread across the phase's existing stage count.

uiElements.label: "+ Add hero" (fallback strip)
uiElements.description: Custom phases only. Sits right of the role lists in the fallback strip and opens the add-hero form in its place (sl-plan-add-hero-form). Save POSTs /api/custom-phases/:key/heroes, appending to the END of the plan (lowest priority in its role), then revalidates the strip, hero grid and Create-all button. Hardcoded phases are not editable.

uiElements.label: "Create all N test sets" button
uiElements.description: Shown above the per-hero plan grid only when at least one hero in the selected phase has no test set yet; creates a test set for every such hero in one click (skips heroes already testing or completed), equivalent to clicking each hero's own Create test set button individually.

uiElements.label: Per-hero DPI plan grid
uiElements.description: Grid of per-hero tiles for the selected phase's plan: sens stages (the one to set now is lit), status, live chunk/minutes line, progress and Remove/Cancel test. This is the only place a hero-tagged active test shows. Progress reads in minutes for Phase 11 onward and games before.

locate.grep: grep -n -F -- 'grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-5 gap-2' client/src/pages/SensLog.tsx

uiElements.label: "Create test set" button (per-hero plan tile)
uiElements.description: Starts a new blind DPI stage-trial set for that specific hero using the plan's preset DPIs and games-per-slot via POST /api/blind/sets.

uiElements.label: Completed status badge
uiElements.description: Overlay badge shown when a hero's plan tile is completed ("Completed" + minutes or games progress), stamped over the tile. The in-progress state and its actions live in sl-plan-status-footer.

uiElements.label: Live sens value (hero tile)
uiElements.description: The stage value of an active test that you set NOW, lit with the accent colour and underline among the tile's sens values; the other values dim while a test runs. Matched from GET /api/blind/state by hero + phase + bracket.

uiElements.label: Live status line (hero tile)
uiElements.description: One line under the sens values on a testing tile: chunk label, blocks left, minutes in the open block (minutes model) or games left in batch (games model); the switch banner and, for game-model sets, Get next stage; DPI only when not the locked 1600.

uiElements.label: "Cancel test" button (plan tile)
uiElements.description: Cancels and deletes the active DPI test set for that hero, prompting for typed confirmation of the game count if games have already been logged.

uiElements.label: "Remove" button (plan tile)
uiElements.description: Removes the hero from the tested pool by pausing its set (POST /api/blind/sets/:id/pause). Nothing is deleted; the hero stops earning credit and drops out of Next test until added back.

uiElements.label: "Add back" button (plan tile, removed hero)
uiElements.description: Returns a removed hero to the tested pool by resuming its paused set (POST /api/blind/sets/:id/resume). The existing set and its credits continue; no new set is created.

uiElements.label: "+ Add new phase" tab button
uiElements.description: Trailing tab after the phase tabs. Opens the sl-add-phase-modal popup pre-filled with the latest phase's heroes instead of switching the displayed plan.

uiElements.label: Add new phase popup form
uiElements.description: Popup (rendered via a React portal into document.body, since the plan card's clip-path would otherwise clip a nested fixed-position modal) for building the next phase's plan. Opens pre-loaded with every hero from the latest phase, each with its sens range auto-narrowed (2/3 of the old gap around the same midpoint) and shown read-only — clicking a row's × excludes that hero. "+ Add hero" appends a blank, fully-editable row for heroes with no prior-phase range to narrow from. Saving appends a new custom phase tab, persisted to localStorage (sl-custom-phases-v1).

uiElements.label: # Stages input (add-phase form)
uiElements.description: Global stage count for the new phase — each hero's auto-narrowed (or manually entered) low/high sens range is evenly spread across this many stage values.

uiElements.label: Add-phase Mouse Acceleration Off toggle
uiElements.description: Sets phaseCurveEnabled=false for the phase about to be created — every hero set built by this modal shares this one on/off value (in_game_sens-style phase-wide constant), not a per-hero or per-match setting.

uiElements.label: Add-phase Mouse Acceleration On toggle
uiElements.description: Sets phaseCurveEnabled=true for the phase about to be created. Same button element as sl-add-phase-curve-enabled-off (mapped from [false, true]) — both ids come from one data-inspect-id template distinguished by the v flag.

uiElements.label: Hero rows list (add-phase form)
uiElements.description: One compact row per hero in the new phase: hero name, archetype, low/high sens (read-only + auto-narrowed for heroes carried over from the latest phase, editable for manually added heroes), games/slot, and an exclude (×) button. The "+ Add hero" row sits at the bottom of this list.

uiElements.label: "+ Add hero" row (add-phase form)
uiElements.description: Dashed-border row at the bottom of the hero list; appends a new blank, fully-editable row (no prior-phase data to auto-narrow from).

uiElements.label: "×" exclude button (add-phase row)
uiElements.description: Removes that hero's row from the new phase being built — the mechanism for excluding a latest-phase hero from the next phase.

uiElements.label: Cancel button (add-phase form)
uiElements.description: Closes the add-phase popup without saving.

uiElements.label: "Create phase" button (add-phase form)
uiElements.description: Builds the new phase tab from the form's rows (spreading each hero's low/high sens across the stage count) and saves it to localStorage, then switches the plan card to the new phase.

uiElements.label: "Load summary" button
uiElements.description: Fetches and displays the final per-stage results table for a completed DPI test set.

uiElements.label: Active DPI/sens stage card
uiElements.description: Compact card for an active test that has no plan tile in any phase tab: a hero-less ad-hoc set, or a hero set whose plan entry no longer matches (activeMatchesTile). Hero-tagged tests are shown by their tile in sl-plan-hero-grid (2026-10-05). Shows stage, the sens to set, restart, and a status line (switch banner or block/minutes progress). Appears only while such a set is active.

uiElements.label: Switch-stages banner
uiElements.description: Amber switch notice on a testing hero tile (sl-plan-live-line) and on the ad-hoc card, shown when the current chunk or batch is complete.

uiElements.label: "Get next stage →" button
uiElements.description: "Get next stage" for a games-model (non-chunked) set whose batch is done. Shown in the hero tile's live line and on the ad-hoc card. Chunked sets switch automatically.

uiElements.label: Auto-switch note
uiElements.description: Shown instead of the advance button on a chunked set when needSwitch is true — tells Sean there's no button, just change the physical setting and log the next match; it auto-credits to the new stage via lib/blind.ts's abbaStageFor. Added 2026-09-23.

uiElements.label: Chunk/block progress line
uiElements.description: Chunk label (A1..B4), blocks left in the stage, and minutes in the open block, for a chunked set. Shown in the hero tile's live line and on the ad-hoc card.

uiElements.label: "Restart test from the beginning" button
uiElements.description: Deletes and restarts the active DPI test set from stage 1, requiring typed confirmation of the game count if games are already logged.

locate.grep: grep -n -F -- 'Restart test from the beginning' client/src/pages/SensLog.tsx

uiElements.label: "Create an ad-hoc sens test set" card
uiElements.description: Form card for manually starting a one-off, hero-less sens stage-trial set outside the phase plan. Mouse DPI is locked at 1600 (sl-locked-dpi-display); each stage's target is an in-game sens value (sl-sens-per-stage-inputs) instead of a DPI value.

locate.grep: grep -n -F -- 'Create an ad-hoc sens test set' client/src/pages/SensLog.tsx

uiElements.label: "# Stages" input
uiElements.description: Number input controlling how many stages the new ad-hoc sens test set will have; resizes the sens-per-stage input list (sl-sens-per-stage-inputs).

uiElements.label: Games per stage (samples) input
uiElements.description: Number input for how many games must be logged per stage before advancing, for the new ad-hoc sens test set.

uiElements.label: Ad-hoc test Mouse Acceleration Off toggle
uiElements.description: Sets curveEnabled=false for the ad-hoc/hero-less test set about to be created via CreateTestCard — a phase-wide constant for this one set, same pattern as the Add-phase modal toggle.

uiElements.label: Ad-hoc test Mouse Acceleration On toggle
uiElements.description: Sets curveEnabled=true for the ad-hoc/hero-less test set about to be created. Same button element as sl-adhoc-curve-enabled-off (mapped from [false, true]).

uiElements.label: "Create test set" button (ad-hoc)
uiElements.description: Submits the ad-hoc DPI test set form, creating a new hero-less test set via POST /api/blind/sets.

uiElements.label: DPI stage results table
uiElements.description: Table of per-stage results (DPI, percent delta, eDPI, equivalent sens at 1600, trial count, feel mean/variance) for a completed DPI test set.

uiElements.label: "Record combat details" section header
uiElements.description: Section header for the backfill area where combat and aim stats are recorded for matches already logged elsewhere.

uiElements.label: Awaiting Stats card

nodes.label: SensAnalysis.tsx
nodes.description: Sensitivity study results dashboard: a data-grounded Recommendation card (verdict + supporting points), a 'What the Data Shows' auto-generated insights card, Feel-vs-Data and Peak-Sens-by-Category scatter charts, Cold-vs-Warm and Adaptation comparison cards, By-Scale and By-Hero tables, and two accuracy box-plot charts (by sens per hero, by hero per sens). uiElements.label: Sens sub-navigation (SensNav)
uiElements.description: Sub-navigation bar rendered at the top of the page, letting the user switch to other pages in the sensitivity-testing section.

uiElements.label: Sensitivity Analysis page header
uiElements.description: Page title and subtitle explaining the page's purpose, rendered above all sensitivity analysis content.

uiElements.label: Sensitivity Analysis page title
uiElements.description: Main page heading 'Sensitivity Analysis' with a one-line subtitle describing what the page shows.

uiElements.label: No aim data yet banner
uiElements.description: Empty-state card shown when no aim data has been logged yet, prompting the user to log matches and record stats on the Enter Stats tab before this page's charts populate.

uiElements.label: No aim data empty-state banner
uiElements.description: Empty-state card shown when no aim data has been logged yet, instructing the user to log matches and record stats on the Enter Stats tab.

uiElements.label: Logged matches / distinct scales summary line
uiElements.description: Text line reporting total logged matches and count of distinct sens scales tested, plus a last-updated timestamp that refreshes whenever a study match's stats are submitted on the Enter Stats tab.

uiElements.label: Match/scale summary line
uiElements.description: Summary text showing total logged matches and distinct sens scales tested, plus a last-updated timestamp that refreshes when new match stats are submitted.

uiElements.label: Standard of measure banner
uiElements.description: Informational banner explaining that every scale on the page is shown as in-game sens at the reference DPI rather than cm/360 or the raw tested DPI.

uiElements.label: Recommendation card
uiElements.description: Card that gives a DPI recommendation and a verdict on whether to keep exploring or start converging, recomputed from the by-scale data below.

uiElements.label: Recommendation verdict badge
uiElements.description: Badge reading 'Narrow focus' or 'Continue testing' depending on whether the leading scale is unbracketed, thin, or close to a runner-up.

uiElements.label: Recommendation verdict badge
uiElements.description: Pill reading 'Narrow focus' or 'Continue testing' inside the Recommendation card, indicating whether the data supports converging on a scale.

uiElements.label: Recommendation supporting points list
uiElements.description: Bulleted list of supporting reasoning points backing the DPI recommendation's verdict.

uiElements.label: What the Data Shows card
uiElements.description: Card presenting an auto-generated plain-language summary of what the charts below show, recomputed every time a match is logged.

uiElements.label: Auto-generated insights list
uiElements.description: Bulleted list of auto-generated insight sentences (best scale by accuracy, win-rate agreement, cold vs warm, adaptation, etc.) inside the What the Data Shows card.

uiElements.label: Feel vs. Data card
uiElements.description: Card containing the Feel vs. Data quadrant chart comparing how fast a scale felt against how it actually performed.

uiElements.label: Feel vs. Data quadrant scatter chart
uiElements.description: Scatter chart plotting each tested sens scale by felt speed (x) vs accuracy delta (y), with crosshair reference lines at the user's own averages splitting the view into four quadrants; hovering a point shows the QuadrantTooltip.

uiElements.label: Peak Sens by Category scatter chart
uiElements.description: Scatter chart plotting one point per category (Overall, Hitscan, Projectile, each hero) at that category's own best-performing sens scale vs. raw accuracy, with a shaded band and reference lines marking scales close to the Overall baseline; hovering a point shows category, sens, accuracy, and delta.

uiElements.label: Peak Sens by Category card
uiElements.description: Card containing the Peak Sens by Category chart showing where each category (Overall, Hitscan, Projectile, each hero) peaks in accuracy.

uiElements.label: Peak Sens by Category verdict badge
uiElements.description: Badge reading 'Split may help', 'One sens fits all', or 'Not enough data' depending on whether tested categories' peak sens values cluster together or scatter apart.

uiElements.label: Peak Sens spread verdict badge
uiElements.description: Pill reading 'Split may help', 'One sens fits all', or 'Not enough data', summarizing whether tested categories' peak sens values cluster together.

uiElements.label: Peak Sens by Category scatter chart
uiElements.description: Scatter chart plotting each category's peak-accuracy sens value with labeled points, a shaded 'close enough to Overall' band, and a baseline mean-accuracy reference line; hovering a point shows the SpreadTooltip.

uiElements.label: Accuracy Over Time card
uiElements.description: Chronological (not scale-aggregated) scatter of every logged point's accuracy delta, colored by which scale was active, with a trailing 8-game rolling-average line — surfaces a practice-effect drift that the rest of the page's scale-aggregated views can't show, since they lose time order entirely.

uiElements.label: Cold vs. Warm card
uiElements.description: Card comparing performance on the first game of a session against later ones, to see whether a sens performs well from the start or only once warmed up.

uiElements.label: Cold vs. Warm stat tile grid
uiElements.description: Grid of stat tiles, one per cold/warm bucket, showing average accuracy, accuracy delta, felt speed, and sample size.

uiElements.label: Cold / Warm stat tiles
uiElements.description: Two stat tiles (Cold, Warm) each showing overall accuracy, accuracy delta vs. baseline, felt speed, and sample size for that bucket.

uiElements.label: Adaptation card
uiElements.description: Card comparing performance just after a sens change versus once settled in, to separate a genuinely worse sens from one not yet adjusted to.

uiElements.label: Adaptation stat tile grid
uiElements.description: Grid of stat tiles, one per fresh/settled bucket, showing average accuracy, accuracy delta, felt speed, and sample size.

uiElements.label: Fresh / Settled stat tiles
uiElements.description: Two stat tiles (fresh-off-a-change, settled) each showing overall accuracy, accuracy delta vs. baseline, felt speed, and sample size for that bucket.

uiElements.label: By Scale table
uiElements.description: Table listing every tested sens scale with eDPI, raw sens, sample size, win rate, overall/crit accuracy, felt speed, and accuracy delta vs baseline.

uiElements.label: By Hero table
uiElements.description: Table listing each tested hero with archetype, sample size, win rate, accuracy, and its optimal sens scale with accuracy deltas.

uiElements.label: Estimated Sweet Spot card
uiElements.description: Fits a weighted quadratic (accuracy delta vs. sens, weighted by games logged) through each category's (Overall + per-hero) tested scales, solved for its vertex — a continuous best-guess optimal sens rather than just whichever tested point scored best. Includes a plotted curve chart (sensAnalysis-curve-fit-chart) for Overall showing the fitted line and actual tested points, above a table with the same read per category. Needs 3+ distinct tested scales per category to fit; each row is annotated good/warn/neutral in plain language depending on fit quality, sample size, whether the fit has an interior peak, and whether that peak falls inside the tested range.

uiElements.label: Estimated Sweet Spot curve chart
uiElements.description: Plots the fitted quadratic curve (Overall only) sampled across the tested sens range, with the actual tested (sens, accuracy delta) points overlaid as dots and the fitted peak marked with a reference line — the curve fit's vertex, previously reported only as a table row, made visible as an actual curve.

uiElements.label: Accuracy by Sens — Per Hero box-plot chart
uiElements.description: Grouped box-plot chart showing accuracy distribution (min/Q1/median/Q3/max) per hero at each tested sens scale, with a hero color-key legend below it.

uiElements.label: Lobby Rank section
uiElements.description: Competitive rank capture at hero select — the tracker's centrepiece. Tracker-owned because it writes lobby_low/lobby_high (and, via the drum, player_rank), which are match columns. The lobby's rank spread is only readable on the opening scoreboard, and a number recalled after the match is a guess, not an observation, so the reading is taken at match start and held in MatchContext (surviving a reload and the log itself). Hidden entirely on Quickplay, which has no rank. One row of two columns: rank drum on the left, lobby spread on the right. Rank and lobby range are stored per account AND per role (8 slots); both are chosen in prematch-identity-strip at the top of the page, not here. Briefly moved into the Log Match form 2026-09-29 and reverted the same night (Sean: it is the centrepiece, and the scoreboard is only readable at hero select). Rendered by the LobbyRankSection component. Prematch.tsx gives it its own full-width card (className "card" inside the #lobby-step wrapper). Since 2026-09-30 that card is the last thing on Pre-Match, after the Select Your Hero row and directly above Log Match's Deaths card (Sean: before hero select it was off screen while he got ready to log deaths, so he kept forgetting it; the in-game scoreboard still shows the lobby ranks then). From 2026-09-29 to 09-30 it sat at game step 4, between the step-1 row and hero select. The map pick now scrolls to the hero advice card in both modes, not to #lobby-step.

uiElements.label: Lobby Rank — drum + track row
